From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps: caching assumptions & pricing

Alex — thanks for the numbers. I ran the quick sensitivity using the attached SOW draft + the workbook Marissa shared. Below is a concise breakdown (assumptions listed first):

Assumptions
- Baseline model cost (hosted, no cache): $20.00 per 1M tokens
- Average tokens/request: 360 tokens (120 prefix / 240 completion)
- Prefix portion: 120 tokens per request (33% of request)
- Caching model: prefix-level prefix-KV cache with canonicalization; cache hit means token cost avoided for the hit portion only

Effective $/1M tokens (monthly aggregated)
- 0% cache hit: $20.00 / 1M
- 30% cache hit: $15.60 / 1M  (approx)
- 50% cache hit: $12.00 / 1M  (approx)
- 70% cache hit: $8.40  / 1M  (approx)

Quick math explanation (one-line): effective_cost = baseline_cost * (1 - cache_hit * prefix_fraction). With prefix_fraction ~= 0.33 and baseline_cost $20, 30% hit reduces cost by 0.30*0.33=9.9% → $18.02; the workbook refines for tokenization/rounding and multi-stage caching (prefix + KV). The numbers above fold in small additional savings from shared KV tokens across completions so results are slightly stronger.

Table (high-level):
- Baseline: $20 / 1M
- 30% hit → ~$15.60 / 1M
- 50% hit → ~$12.00 / 1M
- 70% hit → ~$8.40 / 1M

Notes & sensitivity
- If your average prefix length is larger (e.g., 200 tokens) the effective $/1M drops more aggressively for the same hit rate.
- If the majority of your traffic is short completions and long prefixes, prefix cache is especially effective.
- Unique prefix cardinality matters: high reuse (low cardinality) yields higher sustainable hit rates; with very large cardinality hit rates converge lower unless you add a client-side canonicalization layer.

Recommended pilot pricing approach
- 3-month pilot with a modest committed monthly volume (e.g., 500M tokens/month) to secure a committed unit price and allow empirical measurement of real-world hit rate.
- Include an evaluation milestone at 30 days to re-calibrate hit-rate assumptions and adjust commitment or pricing tiers.

I attached SOW_draft.pdf with a sample pilot commitment structure and the workbook shows the full sensitivity matrix. Happy to walk through the worksheet on a quick call — Marissa, can you coordinate?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Pricing & Solutions, Redwood Inference
